lessons.title: यदि … तर्हि … (yadi … tarhi …) — if, then
lessons.gloss: if … then … — the condition, and what follows from it

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Before the new one: say "if" and "then, in that case". (yadi, tarhi.) You have both words; this chapter puts them to work.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: यदि … तर्हि

segments.text: यदि (yadi), "if", opens the condition; तर्हि (tarhi), "then", opens what follows from it:
यदि वर्षा भवति, yadi varṣā bhavati, तर्हि अहं गृहे तिष्ठामि। tarhi ahaṃ gṛhe tiṣṭhāmi. — "If it rains, I stay at home."
यदि सः आगच्छति, yadi saḥ āgacchati, तर्हि वयं खादामः। tarhi vayaṃ khādāmaḥ. — "If he comes, we eat."

blocks.title: You'll want to know: if not, and the condition second

segments.text: "If not" puts न before the verb of the यदि half:
यदि सः न आगच्छति, yadi saḥ na āgacchati, तर्हि अहं गच्छामि। tarhi ahaṃ gacchāmi. — "If he does not come, I go."
The condition can also come second, with no तर्हि:
अहं गच्छामि, यदि सः न आगच्छति। ahaṃ gacchāmi, yadi saḥ na āgacchati. — "I go if he does not come."

lessons.title: यदि वर्षा भविष्यति (yadi varṣā bhaviṣyati) — if it happens, it will follow
lessons.gloss: if it rains — the future in both halves, or a request after a present condition

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Say "if it rains, I stay at home". (yadi varṣā bhavati, tarhi ahaṃ gṛhe tiṣṭhāmi.) That is what happens every time. Now say what will happen tomorrow.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the future in both halves

segments.text: For one real thing ahead, both halves take the future, as Lanman's vocabulary shows for यदि:
यदि वर्षा भविष्यति, yadi varṣā bhaviṣyati, तर्हि अहं गृहे स्थास्यामि। tarhi ahaṃ gṛhe sthāsyāmi. — "If it rains, I will stay at home."
यदि समयः भविष्यति, yadi samayaḥ bhaviṣyati, तर्हि अहम् आगमिष्यामि। tarhi aham āgamiṣyāmi. — "If there is time, I will come."
यदि भवान् आगमिष्यति, yadi bhavān āgamiṣyati, तर्हि मीरा प्रसन्ना भविष्यति। tarhi mīrā prasannā bhaviṣyati. — "If you come, Mira will be pleased."

blocks.title: You'll want to know: if …, then do this

segments.text: After a condition in the present, the second half can ask or advise, with -तु or -एत्:
यदि भवान् रुग्णः अस्ति, yadi bhavān rugṇaḥ asti, तर्हि वैद्यं गच्छतु। tarhi vaidyaṃ gacchatu. — "If you are ill, please go to the doctor."
यदि धूमयानं गतम्, yadi dhūmayānaṃ gatam, तर्हि भवान् लोकयानेन गच्छेत्। tarhi bhavān lokayānena gacchet. — "If the train has gone, you should go by bus."
लोकयानेन (lokayānena) is "by bus": -ena, "by", as in मतेन.

segments.prompt: Say that if it rains tomorrow you will stay at home, then advise a friend's father to go to the doctor if he is ill.
acceptedResponses: yadi śvaḥ varṣā bhaviṣyati, tarhi ahaṃ gṛhe sthāsyāmi; yadi bhavān rugṇaḥ asti, tarhi vaidyaṃ gacchatu
यदि श्वः वर्षा भविष्यति, तर्हि अहं गृहे स्थास्यामि। यदि भवान् रुग्णः अस्ति, तर्हि वैद्यं गच्छतु।

feedback.correct: The future in both halves for tomorrow; gacchatu for the advice.
feedback.incorrect: Tomorrow's rain: bhaviṣyati, and sthāsyāmi. Advice after a present condition: gacchatu.

segments.source: [PAUSE 3s]

segments.text: "If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home"? (यदि श्वः वर्षा भविष्यति, तर्हि अहं गृहे स्थास्यामि.) Which form goes in both halves? (The future.) "If you are ill, please go to the doctor"? (यदि भवान् रुग्णः अस्ति, तर्हि वैद्यं गच्छतु.)

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Before the new one: say "if there is time, I will come". (yadi samayaḥ bhaviṣyati, tarhi aham āgamiṣyāmi.) Then say "quickly". (śīghram.)
अन्यथा — anyathā — "otherwise": if not, then this.
शीघ्रं गच्छतु, śīghraṃ gacchatu, अन्यथा धूमयानं गमिष्यति। anyathā dhūmayānaṃ gamiṣyati. — "Go quickly, otherwise the train will leave."
कृपया शीघ्रम् आगच्छतु, kṛpayā śīghram āgacchatu, अन्यथा अहं गमिष्यामि। anyathā ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi. — "Please come quickly, otherwise I will leave."

अन्यथा (anyathā) is built on अन्य (anya), "other", with -thā, "in the way of": "in another way". Monier-Williams gives it as "otherwise, in a different manner", and also "in the contrary case", the sense here.
